content.text: This clause set matches the preferred position closely. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 meets the preferred position: renewals are for successive twelve-month (not multi-year) periods, Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is better than our preferred mechanic. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, matching our preferred cap (well inside the 5% fallback), with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The three-year initial term in § 8.1 is the master agreement term rather than an automatic multi-year renewal, so it does not trigger the walk-away test. No redline needed.
